recommended_path: Narrow generator-domain distinction, paired with a strictly-strengthened adjudicator. (1) Generator: reserve disjoint integer value domains — canonical literals draw from pool A, non-canonical lexicals from pool B, each pool-B value having exactly one fixed non-canonical lexical form — so no two generated terms ever collapse onto one reference term anywhere in the dataset (including LOAD documents and their reference INSERT DATA mirrors). Keep the existing INSERT-position-only restriction. Under this invariant the reference normalization is a bijection on terms, solution multisets and fresh-bnode counts agree, and the existing detector absorbs the residual pure-lexical difference exactly as designed. (2) Comparator: adjudicate ONLY when the re-derived normalization is injective and count-preserving. Rationale for rejecting the alternatives: an 'explicit reference-compatibility' path (canonicalizing the reference request stream, or a third sparq instance on a canonicalized stream) does not fix the cascade unless sparq's own stream is also canonicalized — which destroys the very coverage — and adds a new request-rewriting correctness surface. 'Independently checked reference state' can only detect the collapse, and the only sound responses are prevent-it or fail-loudly; disabling comparison for the tainted remainder is forbidden and unsound. No sparq change is warranted. Coverage tradeoff: the corpus loses reference-differential coverage of 'two lexical forms of one value coexisting' and of lexical-driven solution multiplicity; it RETAINS reference coverage of non-canonical lexicals generally (they are still generated, stored, queried and compared). The lost shapes move to sparq-internal oracles where the reference cannot adjudicate — the same tradeoff the module already documents and accepts.
implementation_contract: Generator: single construction helper for integer literals enforcing the disjoint-value invariant; pool-B lexical map fixed and documented. Extend to every datatype the reference encoder canonicalizes, or emit only canonical lexicals for those datatypes.

Comparator: Verdict::AdjudicatedIntegerLexical returned only if ALL hold — (i) normalized line multisets are equal (compare before dedup); (ii) normalization is injective per side (distinct-line count unchanged on each side); (iii) raw quad counts a.len()==b.len(); (iv) distinct blank-node count equal on both sides. Otherwise Verdict::Differs with a message naming the reference-state collapse. This is strictly stronger than today and removes the dedup-induced multiset masking that currently also applies to probe binding sets.
Both changes land together: the comparator change alone increases failures until the generator invariant removes the unadjudicable shape.
